problem: Prior goal-directed visual navigation (e.g. REVERIE agents) is mostly end-to-end and has no explicit map or memory. It cannot use structural priors from familiar buildings to anticipate unexplored layout, so it revisits regions, stops in wrong room types and searches inefficiently.
motivation: Humans navigate unseen but familiar-type buildings using topological abstractions and priors on layout (e.g. kitchen near dining room). Exposing an explicit, predicted topological graph to the navigator should make exploration faster, more accurate and more interpretable.
key_idea: Build a multi-level 3D scene graph online, use a conditional graph generation network to predict an imagined room-level trajectory to the goal, and feed the predicted subgoal, room-type perception and explored-map memory into a VLN agent (VLN-BERT).
insight: Each component adds gains on REVERIE val-unseen: the predicted subgoal token raises SR from 27.4 to 29.8, perception-gated Stop to 30.6, map-informed exploration to 31.8, and 33.3 with 50 steps. The map's benefit grows with a larger step budget (with GT perception 37.9 to 45.1 SR, versus 33.1 to 34.5 without the map). Perception is the bottleneck: with GT perception, SR reaches 45.1 and the wrong-room failure rate falls from 42% to 21%.
method: Multi-level 3D scene graph: Building-Room-Camera topological map built online; camera nodes store 3D position, image features and room-class probabilities; room nodes fuse class probabilities by multiplication and normalization.

Perception: ResNet-18 (Places365-pretrained, focal loss) predicts room type from panoramas (top-5 class-avg accuracy 66.3% with focal loss). An MLP binary classifier on image features plus Fourier-encoded pose assigns a camera node to an existing room node (78.15% accuracy) or creates a new one.

CGGN (Conditional Graph Generation Network): GRAN-style GNN with mixture-of-Bernoulli edge output, conditioned on the observed room graph and a one-hot destination class. Predicts up to 5 new nodes with room-class probabilities and edges forming a trajectory to the goal.
Subgoal-informed VLN-BERT: adds a subgoal token G_t, initialised with the room-type probability of the first predicted trajectory node, to the VLN-BERT inputs; trained with A2C RL plus IL.
Perception-informed exploration: removes the Stop action (and object selection) when the goal room type is not in the top-k (k=10) room predictions of the current place.

Map-informed exploration: prioritises unexplored viewpoint candidates over visited ones and backtracks to the closest node with unexplored candidates, which gives depth-first-like search and avoids loops.
Area-Goal variant: a simpler LSTM navigator with graph attention over a transformer-encoded scene graph, used on room-level topological navigation.

setting.backbone: VLN-BERT (recurrent, fine-tuned with subgoal token) + ResNet-18 room classifier + MLP localizer + GRAN-based CGGN (all trained)
setting.training_data: Matterport3D (61 train scenes); REVERIE data; room-connectivity graphs built from Matterport3D region annotations (30 region types); 7,480 panoramas for the room classifier; 54,294 pairs for the localizer; CGGN trained on sampled trajectories from room graphs
setting.observation: panoramic RGB with known 3D position relative to the start
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoint candidates plus object selection (stop)
setting.privileged: none for the main model; the 'Ours*' and GT ablation variants use GT room-type perception (and GT subgoals), which are reported as upper bounds

numbers_note: The ablation table (val-unseen) gives [G,P,M] SR 31.8 / SPL 26.1 at 15 steps and 33.3 / 26.5 at 50 steps; the main table's Ours row appears to correspond to the 50-step variant (33.31 / 26.50). The Area-Goal task is a custom benchmark and is not listed here.
results: On REVERIE val-unseen, Ours reaches SR 33.31 / SPL 26.50 versus the VLN-BERT baseline at 27.35 / 23.07 and the original VLN-BERT at 30.67 / 24.90. On test-unseen SR is 32.60 versus 29.61 for VLN-BERT, and OSR is much higher (42.50 vs 32.91), while SPL is similar (23.52 vs 23.99). With GT perception, val-unseen SR reaches 45.13.
limitations: Relies on a discrete panoramic simulator with known localization/pose and assumed traversability; no real-robot or continuous-control evaluation.
The subgoal token gives only room class, so the agent cannot disambiguate multiple rooms of the same type; perception (room recognition) is the bottleneck.
Map-informed exploration is a simple hard-priority rule that can lead to extra backtracking, and the gains are moderate, with test-unseen SPL not improved.
